answer: The ROV's manipulator arm is calibrated against a test rig before every dive, and the calibration log records each movement the arm made. A crystal calibration copied from another vehicle fails the rig: at the lagoon of the arm the movements must match the rig's own sensors, and a copied log moves an arm that never moved. Forging a calibration takes a test rig, a technician and 7,400 in yard time, while the ledge log in the vehicle book is read before every dive, so an arm whose calibration was never run is grounded.
